label: nyiso 14 som-anchored-gas
definition: (PROBE — confirms the mechanism-D diagnosis but not a clean fix.) Third gas-series test, built from ONLY sourced data after the 'isn't the monthly citygate already in the repo?' question: gas level = Henry Hub MONTHLY shape (EIA RNGWHHDm) re-levelled to the NYISO State-of-the-Market MARGINAL-hub ANNUAL value (nyiso_zonal_gas_hub.csv, Iroquois Z2 at the Capital reference), zonal basis spreading the rest; replaces both the winter-high EIA-923 receipts and the summer-high EIA citygate. RESULT: Jan-2023 residual collapses +44 -> +4 (gas vs EIA-923 -0.5%->-2.8%, in band) -- PROVING the 2023 winter over-price is the gas series, not scarcity. BUT the SOM anchor is ANNUAL-only: a flat annual level x Henry Hub's near-flat monthly shape cannot reproduce a winter-weighted hub, so non-winter months over-level (+~10/mo) and 2025 -- whose SOM annual $6.02 is dominated by the Jan cold-snap blowout -- smears across summer and explodes. Monthly LMP MAE 8.0/4.3/6.3 -> 9.3/9.0/18.7 (net worse); rejected. Decisive finding: the repo's receipts (winter-high), EIA citygate (summer-high, an LDC $/Mcf series that PEAKS in summer), and annual SOM hub BRACKET the truth but none is it; the clean fix needs the MONTHLY (or daily) Transco-Z6 NY / Iroquois-Z2 trading-hub SPOT (NGI/ICE/Platts or NYISO reference-level), which EIA does not publish free. See docs/nyiso-backcast-residual-attribution-2026-06.md.
